findings.title: $__range queries are now split because interpolation happens before the guard
findings.body: runSplitQuery() now maps request.targets through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() in the chain ending at line 299, before the querySupportsSplitting() partition on line 300. querySupportsSplitting() deliberately returns false for expressions containing $__range via !isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) (line 287), but by the time it runs, $__range has already been replaced with a concrete duration such as '3d'. The guard is therefore dead. For example, count_over_time({job="x"}[$__range]) over a 3-day window will now be split into one-day subqueries while each subquery still carries the full original range vector, which is not equivalent to the intended single unsplit query and can produce incorrect/duplicated metric results. The range-variable decision must be made on the pre-interpolation expression, or an explicit flag must be preserved; the now-stale comment should also be updated.

findings.title: Shard splitting interpolates the same queries twice
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() interpolates every target at line 52, and the resulting splittingTargets are later used to build subRequest (line 154) and passed to runSplitQuery() (line 163). runSplitQuery() now also applies applyTemplateVariables() to each target in its own pipeline (querySplitting.ts lines 296-299). As a result, every sub-query in the shard-splitting path is interpolated twice; the test in this PR now asserts five applyTemplateVariables calls for a single initial target. Plain substitutions may be harmless, but interpolation is not safely idempotent when a substituted value itself contains template syntax such as $... or [[...]], and it is redundant work otherwise. The shard path should avoid re-interpolating already-interpolated targets, or runSplitQuery should support an already-interpolated/internal entry point.
